The must-sees

  • Guggenheim Museum Bilbao

    Museum · 1997

    It opened in 1997 on former docklands and helped turn an industrial city into a cultural destination. The idea that one building can transform a city is now called the Bilbao effect.

    Look for: On the riverside walk, find Maman, Louise Bourgeois’s giant bronze spider, standing on long thin legs.

  • Old Town

    Neighbourhood

    Bilbao was founded here in 1300 by Don Diego López de Haro. Its original core is known as the Seven Streets, Zazpi Kaleak in Basque.

    Look for: Down by the river, the Ribera Market of 1929 is a long hall with stained glass, the old town’s pantry.

  • Plaza Nueva

    Square

    It was completed in the mid-19th century. On Sundays it fills with a market of stamps, coins and old books.

    Look for: One of the arcaded buildings is the home of Euskaltzaindia, the Royal Academy of the Basque Language.

  • Puppy

    Landmark · 1997

    Jeff Koons made the sculpture, and it has stood here since the museum opened in 1997. Its tens of thousands of plants are changed twice a year.

  • Vizcaya Bridge

    Bridge · 1893

    Alberto de Palacio designed it, and it opened in 1893 as the world’s first transporter bridge. A suspended car still ferries people and cars between Portugalete and Getxo, and it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

    Look for: Watch the gondola: it hangs on cables from a trolley that runs along the girder high overhead.

How it works

  1. Open Wizzy in Bilbao and tap Start walk, or pick a ready-made walk.
  2. Put your phone in your pocket. Wizzy runs in the background, even with the screen locked.
  3. When you pass a place, you get a ping. Open it for the story, or keep walking.

Every place you see gets stamped in your Bilbao passport. Your location stays on your phone. No ads, no tracking.
